briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Cannabis Tops $17B as DC and Big Pharma Fast-Track the Future
briefs.top: Michigan's legal cannabis market just crossed $17 billion in lifetime sales and Ann Arbor operators are picking up industry hardware, even as regulators drop the state's biggest-ever fine and a tax-repeal candidate courts the industry ahead of 2026's governor's race. Nationally, momentum is building fast — the FDA is fast-tracking psychedelic medicine, Eli Lilly just closed a major psychedelics acquisition, and DEA/DOJ reviews keep inching cannabis and psilocybin toward the mainstream.

local.text: Michigan cannabis sales cross $17 billion — Combined adult-use and medical sales have topped $17 billion since legal sales began, with August alone generating roughly $259 million in revenue, according to a new state report.

Ann Arbor dispensary lands Best of Detroit honors — Metro Times' 2026 staff picks crowned Information Entropy's converted-church Ann Arbor shop for its flower and live rosin, with Lansing-based edibles brand Captain also singled out for innovation.

GOP governor candidate courts industry on tax repeal — Michigan cannabis operators are rallying behind a Republican gubernatorial hopeful who's made killing the 24% wholesale tax his centerpiece pitch, opening a real political path to relief.

JARS Cannabis becomes Arizona's biggest chain — The Michigan-based dispensary operator sealed a deal to acquire Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa-brand stores, turning a home-state playbook into a major out-of-state expansion.

State drops record fine, clears a bad actor — Regulators hit Muha Meds manufacturer Michigan Investment 10 with a $2 million fine and full license revocation for 'egregious' violations, the toughest enforcement action in state history and a signal the market is cleaning up while tax lawsuits keep pressing forward.

national.text: FDA fast-tracks psychedelic therapies with priority vouchers — The agency issued national priority vouchers to three companies advancing psilocybin and methylone treatments and cleared the first-ever clinical study of an ibogaine derivative.

Eli Lilly closes acquisition of three psychedelic drugs — Lilly's AtaiBeckley deal closed September 11, bringing clinical-stage assets BPL-003, VLS-01 and EMP-01 under a major pharma company's development arm.
DEA advances bid to reschedule psilocybin — A petition to move psilocybin from Schedule I to Schedule II has cleared DEA review and now sits with the Department of Justice.
Court upholds marijuana's Schedule III status — The D.C. Circuit rejected a legal challenge this month and left the federal reclassification of medical marijuana to Schedule III fully in effect.

Curaleaf presses hostile bid for Aurora Cannabis — The MSO's takeover push has triggered a proxy fight pitting America's largest cannabis operator against a Canadian licensed producer, underscoring continued consolidation ambition even as Aurora's board urges shareholders to reject the offer.
